component.name: jellyfin
component.description: TAPPaaS module jellyfin: triage of its own critical/high CVEs (#788). Jellyfin 12.2 (from a pinned nixos-unstable, #850) runs on its NixOS VM (port 8096, plain HTTP), published through the firewall's Caddy to home, netbird and internet zones without the Authentik gate (ADR-032 D3): Jellyfin's own login decides who gets in, and its admin and diagnostic paths answer only inside the site; the library is an NFS share mounted at /media. Live check: the server launches jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 (--ffmpeg flag; FFmpeg 8.1.3, ahead of the nixos-unstable channel, #807), which links libssh 0.12.2, openssl 3.5.8 and, through chromaprint, only libavutil.so.61 of ffmpeg-headless 9.0.1; the Jellyfin process itself runs on the glibc 2.44 and openssl 3.5.8 its .NET runtime brings from nixos-unstable, beside the system's glibc 2.42. jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1's own patches are feature and hardware fixes; FFmpeg 8.1.3 itself fixes most decoder/demuxer CVEs of 8.1.2, the rest are triaged against Jellyfin's own use: library files are attacker-relevant input, so decoder/demuxer CVEs it contains are kept exploitable. Hardware acceleration is none and the VM has no render node. No Live TV tuner and no .strm file are configured. Filter names floodfill/swaprect/hqdn3d/quirc and the spdif format do not occur in Jellyfin 12.2's assemblies.

analysis.detail: GitHub Actions workflow in the jellyfin-ios repository; not part of the Jellyfin server package.
Ubuntu's CUPS AppArmor profile; NixOS ships no such profile and only cups-lib is present (via gtk), no cupsd.

Use-after-free on channel data after close; libssh is linked by jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 as its SFTP client and is reachable only via an sftp:// stream URL. Risk here: low: needs a library .strm with an sftp:// URL to an attacker SSH server; outcome is a crash or UAF in one ffmpeg process. Action: Fixed in a newer libssh; next nixpkgs pin that carries it.

ratings.justification: risk in this deployment, from the triage

analysis.detail: Server-side GSSAPI key-exchange check; libssh is used only as libavformat's SFTP client, and the VM's sshd is OpenSSH.
TIFFReadRGBATile crash; libtiff is only linked by openjpeg/libwebp command-line tools, gdk-pixbuf/gtk4 and opencv, none of which Jellyfin or its ffmpeg load (ffmpeg decodes TIFF natively).
putcontig8bitYCbCr44tile overflow; libtiff is only linked by openjpeg/libwebp tools, gdk-pixbuf/gtk4 and opencv, none of which Jellyfin or its ffmpeg load.
Samba on HP NonStop servers (H06/J06); not this Linux samba build, which is present only as libsmbclient for ffmpeg.

ffmpeg-headless 9.0.1 is in the closure only for chromaprint and pipewire; jellyfin-ffmpeg maps just its libavutil.so.61 (through chromaprint), no running process maps its libavformat, and the RTSP client is in libavformat.
memalign alignment overflow in glibc 2.30 to 2.42 (the CVE's own text); the glibc 2.44 that Jellyfin 12.2's .NET runtime brings from nixos-unstable carries the fix.

strfmon/strfmon_l width-padding overflow, real in glibc 2.44 (loaded by the Jellyfin process through its .NET runtime from nixos-unstable); reachable only through a call to strfmon, and neither the .NET runtime's native libraries, Jellyfin's own, nor jellyfin-ffmpeg and the libraries it links import strfmon (nm -D on the VM).
Packet-buffer retention in OpenSSL's own QUIC stack; nothing on the VM uses it: .NET's HTTP/3 runs on msquic, and Jellyfin and jellyfin-ffmpeg use OpenSSL for TLS over TCP only.
NEW_CONNECTION_ID flood against OpenSSL's own QUIC stack; nothing on the VM uses it (.NET's HTTP/3 runs on msquic; TLS over TCP only).

DTLS handshake retransmission; nothing on the VM speaks DTLS: Jellyfin serves plain HTTP on :8096 (TLS ends at the firewall's Caddy; HTTPS is not enabled in network.xml), outbound HTTPS is TLS over TCP, and ffmpeg's dtls protocol is used only by its WHIP muxer, which Jellyfin never selects.

Needs a TLS server that swaps SSL_CTX mid-handshake between contexts with different providers; Jellyfin serves plain HTTP on :8096 (TLS ends at the firewall's Caddy; HTTPS is not enabled in network.xml), so no process on the VM serves TLS with this OpenSSL.

Signed integer overflow in the MOV/MP4 demuxer's HEIF ispe box (libavformat/mov.c), present in jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1: FFmpeg 8.1.3 does not carry the fix; the box is parsed in any MP4/MOV/HEIF that ffprobe opens. Risk here: medium: needs a crafted file in the library (NFS share writers, media fetched from untrusted sources); playing or probing it needs a Jellyfin login (Sign in with Authentik, Quick Connect or a local account) or a library scan, and the parse runs in a transient ffmpeg as the hardened jellyfin user. Action: fixed upstream in 059eb2e (FFmpeg 9.0), not in 8.1.3; needs a jellyfin-ffmpeg release carrying it, so check the nixpkgs jellyfin-ffmpeg bump.

ratings.justification: risk in this deployment, from the triage

analysis.detail: Out-of-bounds read from unpadded IAMF extradata in the MOV demuxer (mov_read_iacb), present in jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 (not in FFmpeg 8.1.3); any MP4/MOV in the library is probed. Risk here: low: a read past a buffer, not a write; needs a crafted file in the library (NFS share writers, media fetched from untrusted sources); playing or probing it needs a Jellyfin login (Sign in with Authentik, Quick Connect or a local account) or a library scan, and the parse runs in a transient ffmpeg as the hardened jellyfin user. Action: fixed upstream in 8439e02 (FFmpeg 9.0); needs a jellyfin-ffmpeg release carrying it, so check the nixpkgs jellyfin-ffmpeg bump.

ratings.justification: risk in this deployment, from the triage

analysis.detail: Out-of-bounds read from unpadded extradata in the WMA encoder (libavcodec/wmaenc.c), present in jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 (not in FFmpeg 8.1.3); Jellyfin 12.2 lists wmav1/wmav2 among its audio codecs, so a client that asks for WMA audio gets ffmpeg's WMA encoder. Risk here: low: needs a signed-in user whose client requests WMA transcoding (no current Jellyfin client does by default); a read past a buffer in one ffmpeg process. Action: fixed upstream in 23227a4 (FFmpeg 9.0); needs a jellyfin-ffmpeg release carrying it.

ratings.justification: risk in this deployment, from the triage

analysis.detail: RTSP client follows 3xx redirects without a limit (libavformat/rtsp.c), present in jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1; Jellyfin opens rtsp:// only for a .strm or a Live TV source. Risk here: low: no Live TV tuner and no .strm file are configured, so it needs one added that points at an attacker's server, and the outcome is one ffmpeg process spinning. Action: not fixed upstream yet (FFmpeg through 9.0.2).

ratings.justification: risk in this deployment, from the triage

analysis.detail: DVB subtitle parser signed overflow (libavcodec/dvbsub_parser.c): fixed in FFmpeg 8.1.3, which jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 is built on — 46ef25c9c, cherry-picked from 93f2a525e. NVD's range (before 9.0) misses the 8.1 backport.

CineForm HD transform-2 out-of-bounds write (libavcodec/cfhd.c): fixed in FFmpeg 8.1.3, which jellyfin-ffmpeg 8.1.3-1 is built on — ea7210860, cherry-picked from db05df9d1. NVD's range (before 9.0) misses the 8.1 backport.
